### My setup

- MuJoCo 4.0.0 (pip wheel, `mjVERSION_HEADER == 4000000`) with `python/mujoco/rollout.py` from `main` at `01ca66c9`
- Python 3.12, Windows 11

### What's happening

`rollout.rollout` and `Rollout.rollout` are typed and documented as accepting
`Union[mujoco.MjData, Sequence[mujoco.MjData]]`, but the implementation only recognises
`list`:

```python
if not isinstance(data, list):
  data = [data]  # Use a length 1 list to simplify code below
```

A tuple of `MjData` is therefore wrapped into a one-element list and handed to pybind11 as a
tuple, which fails in the compiled rollout with an error that says nothing about the cause.

```python
import numpy as np, mujoco
from mujoco import rollout

xml = '<mujoco><worldbody><body><joint name="j"/><geom size=".1"/></body></worldbody>' \
      '<actuator><motor joint="j"/></actuator></mujoco>'
m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(xml)
d1, d2 = mujoco.MjData(m), mujoco.MjData(m)
initial_state = np.zeros((2, mujoco.mj_stateSize(m, mujoco.mjtState.mjSTATE_FULLPHYSICS)))

rollout.rollout(m, [d1, d2], initial_state, nstep=2)   # works
rollout.rollout(m, (d1, d2), initial_state, nstep=2)   # RuntimeError
```

```
RuntimeError: Unable to cast Python instance of type <class 'tuple'> to C++ type '?'
```

### Expected

Passing any sequence works, matching the annotation and the docstring. A bare `MjData` keeps
meaning a single instance.

I have a one-line-per-site fix plus a regression test that compares the tuple result against
the list result; I will send it as a PR that references this issue.
new_candidates.title: [Python] rollout rejects a tuple of MjData although its signature accepts a Sequence

### Intro

Hi!

I build MJCF models of robot arms from MuJoCo Menagerie parts (an FR3 or a Panda with a Robotiq 2F-85) and use MuJoCo to check them.

### My setup

MuJoCo 4.0.0, also 3.17.0 (the `mujoco` package from PyPI), Python API, Python 3.13.0, x86-64, Windows 10 (10.0.19045). Not tried on Linux.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

When a geom default class sets both `mass="0"` and `density="0"`, so that its geoms add no mass, `to_xml()` in the default `savecompiled="true"` mode saves the class as `<geom type="box"/>`. Both attributes are gone, so in the saved XML the box gets the default density of 1000 and the body's mass goes from 1.666555 to 9.66656.

I expected the saved XML to compile to the same model: "Model Encoding & Saving" says that in both modes "the saved file compiles to the same model". With `spec.compiler.savecompiled = False` it does: the class keeps `mass="0" density="0"` and the mass stays 1.666555.

Either attribute on its own comes through. `density="0"` alone is written in the class, and a `mass` alone is written on each geom that uses the class. With both, neither the class nor the geoms get either one.

A smaller point in the same mode: numbers are written with 6 significant digits (the default precision in `src/xml/xml_numeric_format.cc`), so the sphere's `mass="1.666555"` is saved as `mass="1.66656"`. `savecompiled="false"` writes it exactly.

I ran into this with Menagerie's franka_fr3, whose `collision` class is `<geom type="mesh" group="3" mass="0" density="0"/>` (fr3.xml lines 14-16). Its fr3_link0 has no `<inertial>`, and on 3.17.0 its mass went from 2.82067 kg to 5.81714 kg after a `to_xml()` round trip.

Possibly related: #2478, where `to_xml()` dropped `inertia="shell"` from a mesh default.

### Steps for reproduction

1. Run the code below.
2. It prints the body's mass compiled from the spec (1.666555), then compiled from the XML that `to_xml()` saved (9.66656), then that XML, where the class is `<geom type="box"/>`.
3. The last line is the same round trip with `spec.compiler.savecompiled = False`: 1.666555.

### Minimal model for reproduction

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML
<mujoco>
  <default>
    <default class="collision">
      <geom type="box" mass="0" density="0"/>
    </default>
  </default>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="b">
      <geom class="collision" size="0.1 0.1 0.1"/>
      <geom type="sphere" size="0.05" mass="1.666555"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```
</details>

### Code required for reproduction

```python
import mujoco

xml = """
<mujoco>
  <default>
    <default class="collision">
      <geom type="box" mass="0" density="0"/>
    </default>
  </default>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="b">
      <geom class="collision" size="0.1 0.1 0.1"/>
      <geom type="sphere" size="0.05" mass="1.666555"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
"""

spec = mujoco.MjSpec.from_string(xml)
print(spec.compile().body_mass[1])  # 1.666555
saved = spec.to_xml()
print(mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(saved).body_mass[1])  # 9.66656
print(saved)  # the class is saved as <geom type="box"/>

spec = mujoco.MjSpec.from_string(xml)
spec.compiler.savecompiled = False
saved = spec.to_xml()
print(mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(saved).body_mass[1])  # 1.666555
```

Output on 4.0.0 (the same on 3.17.0):

```
1.666555
9.666560000000002
<mujoco model="MuJoCo Model">
  <compiler angle="radian"/>

  <default>
    <default class="collision">
      <geom type="box"/>
    </default>
  </default>

  <worldbody>
    <body name="b">
      <geom class="collision" size="0.1 0.1 0.1"/>
      <geom size="0.05" mass="1.66656"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>

1.666555
```

### Confirmations

- [X] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting.
- [X] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.
new_candidates.title: to_xml() drops mass="0" density="0" from a geom default class, so the saved XML compiles to a heavier body

### Intro

Hi!

I build MJCF models of robot arms from MuJoCo Menagerie parts (an FR3 or a Panda with a Robotiq 2F-85) and use MuJoCo to check them.

### My setup

MuJoCo 4.0.0, also 3.17.0 (the `mujoco` package from PyPI), Python API, Python 3.13.0, x86-64, Windows 10 (10.0.19045). Not tried on Linux.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

`case2/scene.xml` includes `robot.xml`, which has a `<model>` asset with `file="sub/child.xml"` and attaches it. Loaded as `case2/scene.xml` from the directory that holds `case2`, it fails, with the directory twice in the child's path:

```
XML Error: could not parse model file with error: ParseXML: Error opening file 'case2/case2/sub/child.xml'
```

The same files load the three other ways I tried: `scene.xml` from inside `case2`, `scene.xml` by its absolute path, and `case2/robot.xml` (the robot file itself, without the include) from the directory above. With a `<mesh>` asset in the included file in place of the `<model>`, `case2/scene.xml` loads from the directory above, so it seems specific to `<model>`.

I expected `case2/scene.xml` to load and the child to be found at `case2/sub/child.xml`, as `scene.xml` and `robot.xml` are in the same directory.

Menagerie lays out a scene.xml that includes the robot file, so loading such a scene by a relative path with a directory fails as soon as the robot file attaches a gripper with `<model>` and `<attach>`.

Possibly related: #1772 and #1834, about the paths of other assets in included files.

### Steps for reproduction

1. Run the code below. It writes the three files of the model below into a temporary directory as `case2/scene.xml`, `case2/robot.xml` and `case2/sub/child.xml`, then loads them four ways.
2. The first, `case2/scene.xml` from the directory above `case2`, fails. The other three load.

### Minimal model for reproduction

<details>
<summary>minimal XML (three files)</summary>

`case2/scene.xml`

```XML
<mujoco>
  <include file="robot.xml"/>
</mujoco>
```

`case2/robot.xml`

```XML
<mujoco>
  <asset>
    <model name="child" file="sub/child.xml"/>
  </asset>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="b">
      <geom size="0.1"/>
      <attach model="child" body="c" prefix="x_"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```

`case2/sub/child.xml`

```XML
<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="c">
      <geom size="0.05"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```
</details>

### Code required for reproduction

```python
import os
import tempfile

import mujoco

files = {
    "case2/scene.xml": """<mujoco>
  <include file="robot.xml"/>
</mujoco>""",
    "case2/robot.xml": """<mujoco>
  <asset>
    <model name="child" file="sub/child.xml"/>
  </asset>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="b">
      <geom size="0.1"/>
      <attach model="child" body="c" prefix="x_"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>""",
    "case2/sub/child.xml": """<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <body name="c">
      <geom size="0.05"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>""",
}
root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
for name, text in files.items():
  path = os.path.join(root, name)
  os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
  with open(path, "w") as f:
    f.write(text)


def load(label, path, cwd):
  os.chdir(cwd)
  try:
    mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(path)
    print("ok   ", label)
  except Exception as e:
    print("FAILS", label, "->", str(e).strip().splitlines()[0])


load("case2/scene.xml from the parent dir", "case2/scene.xml", root)
load("case2/robot.xml from the parent dir", "case2/robot.xml", root)
load("scene.xml from inside case2", "scene.xml", os.path.join(root, "case2"))
load("scene.xml by its absolute path", os.path.join(root, "case2", "scene.xml"), root)
```

Output on 4.0.0 (the same on 3.17.0):

```
FAILS case2/scene.xml from the parent dir -> XML Error: could not parse model file with error: ParseXML: Error opening file 'case2/case2/sub/child.xml'
ok    case2/robot.xml from the parent dir
ok    scene.xml from inside case2
ok    scene.xml by its absolute path
```

### Confirmations

- [X] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting.
- [X] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.

### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
- LeRobot version: 0.7.0
- Platform: macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O (Apple M3 Max)
- Python version: 3.13.14
- Huggingface Hub version: 2.4.0
- Datasets version: 5.1.0
- Numpy version: 2.2.6
- FFmpeg version: 9.0.2
- PyTorch version: 2.15.0
- Torchcodec version: 0.17.0
- PyAV version: 15.1.0 (bundles SVT-AV1 3.0.0)
```

### Description

On macOS on Apple silicon, a process that encodes video with LeRobot's default encoder (`libsvtav1`) can be killed by SIGTRAP when an encoder closes at the end of an episode. It shows up as exit code 133 or `zsh: trace trap`, with no Python traceback. The kill happens in `lerobot-record` and in any `LeRobotDataset` writer, with or without `streaming_encoding`.

In our runs about 0.1 to 0.4% of encoder closes crashed, most often for short episodes. When it happens during recording, the process loses every episode it hasn't finished writing.

The cause is a bug in SVT-AV1, not in LeRobot:
- **The race:** when an encoder shuts down, a race can leave SVT-AV1's `ref_buffer_available_semaphore` one count below its starting value.
- **Why only macOS:** Apple's libdispatch traps when a semaphore is freed below its starting value. Linux and Windows semaphores don't check, so the bug is harmless there.
- **Upstream:** it's reported as AOMediaCodec/SVT-AV1#2961 and fixed by https://github.com/AOMediaCodec/SVT-AV1/commit/049193fc0e16ba7f1afe8baa51292157b681cb2a, which was released in SVT-AV1 4.3.0 on 2026-11-01.

LeRobot can't pick up that fix yet:
- LeRobot pins `av>=15,<16`, and PyAV 15.1.0 bundles SVT-AV1 3.0.0.
- No PyAV release bundles 4.3.0 yet. 19.0.2 has 4.2.0, which is still affected. PyAV's FFmpeg builds (pyav-ffmpeg) moved to SVT-AV1 4.3.0 on 2026-11-02, so the next PyAV release will probably include the fix.

LeRobot's encoder teardown is correct. `_CameraEncoderThread` sends end of stream, drains the encoder and closes it on its own thread.

### Context & Reproduction

The script below opens, encodes and closes two `libsvtav1` encoders at a time with `RGBEncoderConfig()`'s default options, the way two camera encoder threads finish an episode:

```python
import tempfile
import threading
from pathlib import Path

import av
import numpy as np
from lerobot.configs.video import RGBEncoderConfig

options = RGBEncoderConfig().get_codec_options(encoder_threads=2, as_strings=True)
frame = np.zeros((48, 64, 3), np.uint8)


def encode(path: Path, frames: int) -> None:
    out = av.open(str(path), "w")
    stream = out.add_stream("libsvtav1", 30, options=options)
    stream.width, stream.height, stream.pix_fmt = 64, 48, "yuv420p"
    for _ in range(frames):
        out.mux(stream.encode(av.VideoFrame.from_ndarray(frame, format="rgb24")))
    out.mux(stream.encode())
    out.close()


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    for cycle in range(5000):
        threads = [threading.Thread(target=encode, args=(Path(tmp) / f"{i}.mp4", 1 + cycle % 3)) for i in range(2)]
        for t in threads:
            t.start()
        for t in threads:
            t.join()
        if cycle % 250 == 0:
            print(f"{2 * cycle} encoder closes", flush=True)
print("no crash")
```

I ran it 3 times on an M3 Max:
- 2 runs died with exit code 133, after fewer than 500 and fewer than 1,000 encoder closes;
- 1 run finished 10,000 closes without a crash.

Over longer stress runs, 134 of 36,000 encoder closes crashed.

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell
Exception Type:  EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
Application Specific Information:
  BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBDISPATCH: Semaphore object deallocated while in use (current value < original value)
  Abort Cause 1

Crashed Thread:
0  libdispatch.dylib          _dispatch_semaphore_dispose.cold.1
1  libdispatch.dylib          _dispatch_semaphore_dispose
2  libdispatch.dylib          _dispatch_dispose
3  libdispatch.dylib          dispatch_release
4  libSvtAv1Enc.3.0.0.dylib   svt_destroy_semaphore
5  libSvtAv1Enc.3.0.0.dylib   svt_sequence_control_set_instance_dctor
6  libSvtAv1Enc.3.0.0.dylib   svt_enc_handle_dctor
7  libSvtAv1Enc.3.0.0.dylib   svt_av1_enc_deinit_handle
8  libavcodec.61.19.101.dylib
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch. (`main` still pins `av>=15.0.0,<16.0.0`.)
- [ ] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem. (It is specific to macOS: the same race is harmless on Linux and Windows.)

### Additional Info / Workarounds

**Suggested fix:** allow a PyAV that bundles SVT-AV1 4.3.0 or later, once one is released. Moving the pin past av 17.0 needs a code change first:
- PyAV 17.1 removed `av.option` and `Codec.descriptor`;
- `lerobot/datasets/pyav_utils.py` uses both (the `-> dict[str, av.option.Option]` annotation and `codec.descriptor.options`);
- so with av 19.0.2, `import lerobot.datasets` fails with `AttributeError: module 'av' has no attribute 'option'`.

**Workarounds until then:**

1. **Record with another encoder.** For example `--dataset.rgb_encoder.vcodec=h264_videotoolbox` or `libx264`, which don't use SVT-AV1.
2. **Apply SVT-AV1's fix at runtime.** This keeps AV1. The library below does what commit 049193fc does, but only for semaphores that SVT-AV1 creates.
   - Build it with `cc -dynamiclib -O2 -o libsvtsem.dylib svtsem.c`.
   - Start Python with `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=/path/to/libsvtsem.dylib`. Children inherit it, except through `/bin/sh`, which strips `DYLD_*` variables.
   - In our stress runs it took crashes from 175 in 92,000 encoder closes to 0 in 92,000, and the encoded video stream is byte-identical.

<details><summary>svtsem.c</summary>

```c
// Applies SVT-AV1 commit 049193fc at runtime: semaphores that libSvtAv1Enc creates with a count
// above 0 are created at 0 and signalled up to that count, so libdispatch's dispose check compares
// against 0. Load with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES.
#include <dispatch/dispatch.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <string.h>

static int from_svt(const void *caller) {
    Dl_info info;
    return dladdr(caller, &info) && info.dli_fname && strstr(info.dli_fname, "libSvtAv1Enc");
}

dispatch_semaphore_t svtsem_create(intptr_t value) {
    if (value > 0 && from_svt(__builtin_return_address(0))) {
        dispatch_semaphore_t semaphore = dispatch_semaphore_create(0);  // calls from this library aren't interposed
        for (intptr_t i = 0; semaphore && i < value; i++) dispatch_semaphore_signal(semaphore);
        return semaphore;
    }
    return dispatch_semaphore_create(value);
}

__attribute__((used, section("__DATA,__interpose"))) static const struct {
    const void *replacement;
    const void *original;
} interpose_semaphore_create = {(const void *)svtsem_create, (const void *)dispatch_semaphore_create};
```

</details>
new_candidates.title: macOS: recording dies with SIGTRAP (exit 133) when an SVT-AV1 encoder closes (bundled SVT-AV1 3.0.0 bug, fixed in 4.3.0)

new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
- LeRobot version: 0.7.0
- Platform: macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O (Apple M3 Max)
- Python version: 3.13.14
- PyAV version: 15.1.0
```

### Description

For `h264_videotoolbox` and `hevc_videotoolbox`, which `vcodec="auto"` picks on macOS, `VideoEncoderConfig.get_codec_options` turns `crf` into `{"q:v": 100 - 2 * crf}` (`lerobot/configs/video.py`).

`q:v` is an option of the `ffmpeg` command line, not of the codec. PyAV hands the options dict to the codec, and FFmpeg silently ignores a key the codec doesn't know. So `crf` has no effect, and VideoToolbox picks its own bitrate.

I measured this on 20 s of 640×480, 30 fps camera footage with `g=2`. Encoding with `crf` 30, 20 and 12 (`q:v` 40, 60 and 76) produced the same video: 4.5 Mbps and VMAF 85.6 each time. The files differ only in the MP4 header's creation time, and they decode to identical frames.

VideoToolbox's quality setting is reached through `global_quality` with the `qscale` flag. FFmpeg's `videotoolboxenc.c` reads `avctx->global_quality / FF_QP2LAMBDA` when `AV_CODEC_FLAG_QSCALE` is set. With those options the quality does change:

| Options | Front camera, Mbps | VMAF |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `q:v` 40, 60 or 76 (current mapping) | 4.48 (the same video) | 85.6 |
| `flags=+qscale`, `global_quality=50*118` | 1.13 | 75.4 |
| `flags=+qscale`, `global_quality=70*118` | 2.98 | 84.6 |
| `flags=+qscale`, `global_quality=80*118` | 4.67 | 86.1 |

### Context & Reproduction

```python
import av, numpy as np
from lerobot.configs.video import RGBEncoderConfig

frames = [np.random.default_rng(i).integers(0, 255, (480, 640, 3), np.uint8) for i in range(60)]
for crf in (30, 20, 12):
    cfg = RGBEncoderConfig(vcodec="h264_videotoolbox", crf=crf)
    out = av.open(f"vt_crf{crf}.mp4", "w")
    s = out.add_stream(cfg.vcodec, 30, options=cfg.get_codec_options(as_strings=True))
    s.width, s.height, s.pix_fmt = 640, 480, "yuv420p"
    for a in frames:
        out.mux(s.encode(av.VideoFrame.from_ndarray(a, format="rgb24")))
    out.mux(s.encode())
    out.close()
# All three decode to identical frames: ffmpeg -v error -i vt_crf30.mp4 -f md5 - (and the same for 20 and 12)
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [ ] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem. (VideoToolbox exists only on macOS.)

### Additional Info / Workarounds

**Suggested fix:** for the VideoToolbox encoders, map `crf` to `{"flags": "+qscale", "global_quality": str(q * 118)}` (118 is `FF_QP2LAMBDA`) instead of `q:v`.

**Workaround today:** pass those two keys through `extra_options`, with `crf=None`.
